On the morning of November 6, 2026, a public lecture on the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, themed "Neutrinos from Beyond the Milky Way," was held at the Faculty of Science, Vietnam National University, Hanoi.

This event marks the beginning of a series of public lectures for this academic year, leading up to the 70th anniversary of the Hanoi University of Science , Vietnam National University, Hanoi.

The program was organized by the Executive Board of the Talented Bachelor of Science Program in collaboration with the Department of Physics. The event attracted a large number of faculty members, young researchers, and students from the university.

Associate Professor Dr. Nguyen Mau Chung is giving a lecture in a public lecture program about the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics.

The speaker for this lecture is Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nguyen Mau Chung, Department of Physics, Faculty of Science - Vietnam National University, Hanoi.

During the lecture, Associate Professor Dr. Nguyen Mau Chung shared interesting scientific content about high-energy neutrinos, the IceCube observatory in Antarctica, and discoveries that open up new research directions in the high-energy universe – neutrino astronomy.

Through the story of IceCube and its journey to find neutrinos from beyond the Milky Way, the lecture brings attendees closer to modern scientific issues while exploring how humanity is gradually unraveling the mysteries of the universe.

Associate Professor Dr. Nguyen Mau Chung, born in 1957, is a former student of the Class of 19 at Hanoi University. He defended his doctoral dissertation at the University of Lausanne, Switzerland , and is one of the few Vietnamese scientists working at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN).

During the 2010s, Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nguyen Mau Chung and his research group contributed a significant number of scientific research papers in physics. These contributions were one of the important factors contributing to the high ranking of the Physics department at the Faculty of Science in particular and at Vietnam National University, Hanoi in general.

The discussion was lively, with many questions from students and faculty members of the Physics Department. Associate Professor Dr. Nguyen Mau Trung provided detailed answers and further inspired a passion for science in the young students.

The organizers presented flowers to thank Associate Professor Dr. Nguyen Mau Trung after he finished his lecture.

The first public lecture program of the 2026-2027 academic year has concluded, leaving many profound impressions and inspiring a spirit of dedication to scientific exploration and discovery among the young generation of the University of Science.
